source.title: Learning with Noisy Ground Truth: From 2D Classification to 3D Reconstruction

record.file_problem: Full text supplied. It is a survey, with some observations and figures; many cited results are prior work.
record.tranche_reason: The survey reports observations about fitting mislabeled training examples and later test degradation, which bear on the noisy-label version of the claim. It does not reproduce the original random-label experiment.
record.gate_note: The paper discusses random-label memorization through its citation of Zhang et al. (2018), but cited findings are not rows. Its own reported observations concern partially corrupted labels and noisy 3D scenes. Figure 1's CE+EM comparison is not extracted because the reported confidence stability does not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: Despite being a survey, the paper reports its own classification illustrations: prediction trajectories at 40% label noise and loss distributions at 60% noise. These bear on V6's learning order and V4's eventual training-set fit.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate but incomplete. The authors emphasize early learning of clean structure followed by noisy-target memorization, connect this behavior to distractor fitting in 3D reconstruction, and illustrate dynamic masking. They also propose a unified LNGT definition and an error-decomposition taxonomy for existing methods.
record.recipe_differences: Survey discussion and illustrative observations on noisy-label training; not a reproduction of the original random-label experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper describes different behavior over training: clean samples tend to have smaller losses early, while later training can fit mislabeled samples. It also contrasts CE with CE+EM confidence trajectories in Figure 1, which do not measure the claim versions directly.

fits_no_version.finding: The prose reports later test-performance degradation at a fixed corruption fraction, without a test curve or numerical measurement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Continued CE training on noisy labels can worsen generalization after earlier training.

fits_no_version.finding: CE+EM produces more stable prediction probabilities than vanilla CE in Figure 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Entropy minimization can stabilize predictions during noisy-label training.

fits_no_version.finding: Mip-NeRF 360 initially fits clean scene pixels and later fits distractors; dynamic masking suppresses distractor fitting.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scene reconstruction can learn persistent scene content before transient distractor pixels.

record.problems: The results relevant to V4 are described without numerical training or test errors, and only at stated noise fractions of 40% and 60%; no full noise-rate sweep or uncertainty is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Figure 3's 3D scene observations concern distractor pixels rather than the claim versions and are described under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, near-zero training error in that setting, chance test performance, and unchanged architecture and hyperparameters.
Training-time ratios and convergence changes across corruption fractions.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.
A corruption sweep from none to all, perfect fitting throughout that sweep, and steadily increasing test error toward chance. The noise-generation mechanism is not specified for the illustrations.
Effects of weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting, and generalization after removing them.
A separate fully random-label training condition and quantitative comparisons of learning times.

missing.what: Record the authors' ResNet34 learning-order observation: clean and mislabeled normalized-loss distributions initially overlap, separate early, and merge again later as mislabeled samples are fitted. The text also identifies epoch 45 as a stage with useful true-class estimates for noisy samples.
missing.locator: Section 2.1, Figure 2 caption and accompanying discussion

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports V6 more directly than the record recognizes. Missing coverage of V4's noise-rate sweep is an untested part, not evidence that the claim fails. No numerical errors or unreadable figure values are inferred.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training on a completely random labeling, test error at chance, or whether architecture and hyperparameters were unchanged.
No comparison of training time or convergence rate across label-noise fractions.
No experiments on shuffled pixels or Gaussian-noise inputs.
The survey reports observations at 40% and 60% label noise, not a sweep from none to all; it does not report a steady test-error curve or quantify capture of remaining signal.
No direct test of weight decay, dropout, data augmentation, or their removal.

It notes that clean samples tend to have smaller loss early, but does not test whether shared real-data patterns are learned before noisy labels or compare learning of real versus random labels over training.

rows.subject: 8-layer CNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained with cross-entropy on CIFAR-10 with 40% label noise; the text describes output probabilities through training.
rows.measure: Output probabilities for noisy and latent true labels; the text says the model memorizes wrong labels and test performance degrades later in training.
rows.value: The text reports large oscillations during vanilla CE training and later memorization of wrong labels with degraded test performance.
rows.note: The description is for a single noise fraction and does not quantify test error.
rows.check: Figure 1 and its discussion are in the introduction, not Section 2.1. The relevant result is an initially correct prediction on a mislabeled deer image followed by learning its incorrect horse label. This bears on learning order, not test error across corruption fractions. Remove the unmeasured test-performance claim from this row; confidence oscillations alone do not establish a claim version.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with 60% noise using cross-entropy; the text reports eventual fitting of mislabeled training samples.
rows.value: The DNNs completely fit the training set including mislabeled samples eventually.
rows.note: The prose states this as a general observation and refers to Figure 2; it does not give a numerical training error.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports eventual complete fitting, including mislabeled samples, and points to Figure 2. Thus the measured fitting component is observed, rather than partial. Figure 2 displays normalized loss distributions, not numerical training error; the precise corruption mechanism is unspecified.

rows.subject: ResNet34
rows.operation_detail: Trained on CIFAR-10 with 60% noise using cross-entropy; the text reports later test-performance degradation.
rows.value: Test performance degradation in the later stage of training.
rows.note: No test-error value or trajectory is stated.
rows.check: Later test degradation during training at a fixed noise fraction does not measure V4's test-error increase across noise fractions. Figure 2 contains loss distributions, not test-performance curves. The prose states degradation generally without a model-specific test measurement.

relationships.condition: ResNet34 trained with CE on CIFAR-10 at 60% label noise; eventual training-set fit
relationships.reason: R2 records the explicit report of complete fitting, including mislabeled samples; the untested corruption sweep does not justify a limits_scope verdict.
relationships.display_finding: Training eventually fit the entire dataset, including mislabeled samples.

relationships.condition: Vanilla CE classification on CIFAR-10 with 40% and 60% label noise
relationships.reason: R1 describes correct-class prediction preceding incorrect-label memorization; Section 2.1 and Figure 2 additionally report early clean/noisy loss separation followed by merging, a result missing from the rows.
relationships.display_finding: Correct-class predictions preceded incorrect-label memorization, while initially separated clean and noisy loss distributions later merged.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The text reports later memorization and test degradation, but does not establish perfect fit plus a steadily rising test error across noise fractions (R1–R3).
